updates.name: Antonio Celis-Murillo
updates.bio: Heads the USGS Bird Banding Laboratory at the Eastern Ecological Science Center in Laurel, Maryland, overseeing a century-long archive of North American banding records, federal banding permits, and the linking of banding with tracking data. He was earlier a BBL biologist at Patuxent Wildlife Research Center and a postdoc at the Illinois Natural History Survey; PhD, University of Illinois (2015).
updates.research_interests: bird banding; avian migration; migratory bird ecology; movement ecology; bioacoustics; biomonitoring and biosurveillance; community science; data management
updates.current_affiliation: U.S. Geological Survey, Eastern Ecological Science Center

updates.name: Aubrey K. Bunch
updates.bio: Supervisory biologist in Indianapolis with the USGS's Ohio-Kentucky-Indiana Water Science Center, where she has worked since 2011 and leads the Ecosystem Science Section's water-quality and ecological projects. Her listed expertise is nutrient loads; her Ball State University MS thesis examined nonprescription pharmaceuticals in central Indiana streams.
updates.research_interests: nutrient loads; aquatic ecosystems and water quality; pharmaceuticals in streams

updates.name: Becky Nichols
updates.bio: Long-serving park entomologist at Great Smoky Mountains National Park, hired in 1998. For nearly three decades she has sampled stream aquatic insects for the park's Inventory and Monitoring program, uses degree-day data to forecast synchronous firefly emergence, and works with Discover Life in America on the All Taxa Biodiversity Inventory. PhD, University of Missouri.
updates.research_interests: aquatic insect monitoring of park streams (Inventory and Monitoring); synchronous firefly (Photinus carolinus) emergence timing; All Taxa Biodiversity Inventory; insect biodiversity
updates.evidence: Becky Nichols, the park's long-time entomologist
updates.notes: The source is a Smokies Life (park partner) article dated 2026-02-12. No NPS staff page was found, so homepage_url stays null. The stored ORCID 0000-0001-5692-8754 has the name Becky Nichols but no employment on record, so it is neither confirmed nor changed.

updates.name: Bernard R. Kuhajda
updates.bio: Fish biologist with the Tennessee Aquarium Conservation Institute since 2012. He previously spent a quarter century at the University of Alabama, curating a museum collection of roughly one million preserved fish specimens. His specialty is surveying and monitoring threatened and endangered aquatic species in the Southeast, and he serves on several USFWS recovery teams.
updates.research_interests: surveying and monitoring threatened and endangered aquatic species of the southeastern U.S.; evaluating the effectiveness of conservation programs; endangered species recovery; freshwater fishes

updates.name: Beth A. Newingham
updates.bio: Reno-based research ecologist for USDA's Agricultural Research Service, also serving as adjunct faculty at the University of Nevada, Reno. Her work spans plant community, soil, ecosystem, fire and restoration ecology as well as climate change, with special interest in how plant and soil processes are linked.

updates.name: Brian L. McGlynn
updates.bio: Adjunct professor in the Earth and Climate Sciences Division of Duke University's Nicholas School of the Environment. His field studies examine how hydrological and ecological processes scale through space and time in intact and disturbed watersheds and stream networks, including NSF-funded work on mountaintop-mining impacts, stream biomes and the Calhoun Critical Zone Observatory. PhD, SUNY-ESF (2002).
updates.research_interests: spatial and temporal scaling of hydrological and ecological processes; watershed hydrology and biogeochemistry; stream networks; mountaintop mining effects on watersheds; critical zone dynamics
updates.current_affiliation: Duke University, Nicholas School of the Environment (Earth & Climate Sciences Division)

updates.name: Bruce Peterjohn
updates.bio: Retired wildlife biologist who was the eighth chief of the USGS Bird Banding Laboratory at Patuxent Wildlife Research Center from 2008 until retiring at the end of 2019. He joined Patuxent in 1991 with the North American Breeding Bird Survey, built point-count and breeding-bird-atlas data systems, and authored studies of avian population trends using survey data.
updates.research_interests: North American Breeding Bird Survey; avian population trends; bird monitoring databases; bird banding; wintering hummingbirds

updates.name: Bryan A. Franz
updates.bio: Holds a research scientist post in NASA Goddard's Ocean Ecology Laboratory, where he is assistant chief for science research; he has worked on satellite ocean color since 1996. He is deputy manager of NASA's Ocean Biology Processing Group and manages the PACE mission's Science Data Segment, and built the processing software and vicarious calibration behind NASA's global ocean color products.
updates.research_interests: satellite ocean color remote sensing; ocean biology and biogeochemistry; atmospheric correction; bio-optical algorithms and inherent optical property inversion; vicarious calibration and sensor cross-calibration; PACE mission science data processing

updates.name: Bryan L. Foster
updates.bio: Plant community ecologist who became director of Michigan State University's W.K. Kellogg Biological Station in November 2025 and is a professor of plant biology there. He joined the University of Kansas ecology and evolutionary biology faculty in 1999, ran long-term grassland experiments, and led its field station between 2018 and 2025.
updates.research_interests: plant community structure and function; biotic interactions, resource conditions and species pools; global change impacts on biodiversity (habitat fragmentation, nutrient enrichment, exotic species, disturbance); conservation and restoration of native plant communities; grassland dynamics
updates.current_title: Director, W.K. Kellogg Biological Station; Professor, Department of Plant Biology
